show_title: GLIDE: A Fairytale in Twelve Weeks
logline: On a rushed October school morning, Mae, a hand surgeon, won't let her daughter cut her own bagel. Then she cuts it herself, held in the palm of her left hand. Every patient has heard her lecture against doing exactly that. The knife cuts the deep flexor tendon of her ring finger in Zone Two, No Man's Land, and divides a couple so long married that they had forgotten they were two. PROX, the forearm King's daughter, is dragged back into the dark palm by her father. TIP, the fingertip's boy, slides away towards the end of the world. A surgeon Mae trained stitches them back together. Then they have twelve weeks to learn to GLIDE. If the King pulls too hard, they tear. If they hold too still, they belong to Scarlett Adhesion, the honey-voiced scar who purrs that nothing tears if nothing moves.
world:
The whole show takes place inside the LEFT hand of MAE, a right-handed hand surgeon in her late thirties and a busy mum. The kingdom calls itself 'the holding hand'. It holds the coffee, the phone, the steering wheel, the bagel and Wren. The hand is a small fairytale kingdom with proud, slightly smug, medically literate people, because their hand has mended a thousand other hands.

PLACES: Up in the forearm stands the castle of KING PROFUNDUS, the flexor digitorum profundus muscle belly, who rules by pulling. He has three daughters in the middle, ring and little fingers who share one muscle belly, so when one is held back the others can't fully close either (the quadriga effect). The heroine is the ring-finger daughter, PROX. Down the finger runs a glistening tunnel, the sheath, which is wet with the fluid that feeds a moving tendon. Five ring-shaped PULLEYS, A1 to A5, hold the tendon to the bone; without them it would 'bowstring' off the bone like a loose string. BIG SISTER SUPERFICIALIS (FDS, never a singing role) splits around Prox at Camper's chiasm, hugs her from underneath, rejoins behind her and anchors on the middle bone. Between the distal palm crease (the A1 pulley) and Big Sister's anchor lies ZONE TWO, which old Doctor Bunnell's map calls NO MAN'S LAND. The tunnel is tight there, and SCARLETT ADHESION moves into any space that stops moving.

THE COUPLE: The tendon was always two characters, long married. PROX is the King's daughter, running from the forearm through the palm into the finger. TIP is 'the fingertip's boy', anchored on the tiny bone at the end of the world (the distal phalanx). They were joined so long ago that the kingdom says their names as one word, 'Proxantip', and they forgot they were two. Only Tip bends the very tip of the finger, and only when Prox pulls; he has never moved by himself.

THE INJURY (accurate on purpose): Mae is right-handed, so she holds the bagel in her left palm with the ring finger CURLED round it and saws with her right hand. The knife enters distal Zone Two, past Camper's chiasm. Big Sister is wrapped BENEATH Prox there, so only Prox is cut. Because the finger was bent, the tendon cut lies further down than the skin cut. When Mae opens her hand, Tip slides away down the finger towards the A4 pulley, and the King's recoil drags Prox back into the palm. She stops there and not at the wrist because LUMBO, the little worm-shaped lumbrical muscle, grows from her side and holds on. DIGBY, the digital nerve on the ulnar side of the finger, is cut too, so half the finger pulp goes quiet.

HEALING BIOLOGY AS FAIRYTALE: A moving tendon is fed by the tunnel's fluid and mends 'from the inside' (intrinsic healing). A still one gets 'builders' sent in from the tunnel walls (extrinsic healing by fibroblasts), and those are Scarlett's army, THE FIBROBLASTS, who lay down messy Type Three collagen 'every which way'. Swelling is her advance guard ('swelling is glue'). Healing needs scar. The question is only which way it points.

HUMANS: They are heard only as voices from Above, closer and drier than the kingdom's fairytale reverb. MAE is the patient, surgeon and mother. WREN is her small daughter. DR. TEO OKAFOR, whom Mae trained, does the repair. THEA the hand therapist is a fairy godmother: her splint pan is a cauldron, plaster becomes thermoplastic like a pumpkin becoming a carriage, and her goniometer is her 'wand'.

TIMELINE (sung as time stamps): Day 0 is a Tuesday school morning in mid-October. Day 2: the wide-awake (WALANT) repair, after which she goes home in a plaster backslab. Day 3: the thermoplastic dorsal blocking splint and the rules. Day 10: skin stitches out, and the near-tear on the stairs. Weeks 3 to 6: Mae lies at clinic and Scarlett reigns. Weeks 4 to 6: Digby's tingle advances; the splint comes off at six weeks, and the fingertip won't bend. Week 8: the dark night and the first flicker. Week 12: a January morning, the first day of the new term, the school gate.

characters.name: PROX (Proxima)
characters.who: The heroine. She is King Profundus's ring-finger daughter, the proximal part of the deep flexor tendon, still attached to her father's muscle. She is brave, impatient and devoted, and a puller by birth. She is the only one in the kingdom who can talk to the King, and the King is the only one who can actually pull. Her agency is her negotiation with her father: she refuses his 'come home' (Song 2), fails to stop his all-out grab (Song 6), fails to unfreeze his vow (Song 7), and finally TEACHES him the whisper Thea prescribed (Song 9).
characters.want: Song 2: to get back to Tip. Song 5, after the reunion, Thea changes it: to GLIDE with him, not just be stitched to him. Her hidden arc: neither pulling hard (tear) nor holding still (glue) keeps him; a gentle pull every day, a little further each time, does.
characters.voice: PROX - bright clear young mezzo-soprano, warm chest belt, earnest storybook-heroine tone, breathy tenderness in quiet verses

characters.name: TIP
characters.who: The love interest. He is 'the fingertip's boy', the distal part of the tendon, anchored to the fingertip bone at the end of the world. He has been married to Prox since before Mae could crawl. He is funny, with a fingertip's vanity ('I'm the bit that touches EVERYTHING. Phones. Noses. I've been in a bagel.'), loyal, and secretly terrified, because he has never once moved by himself. After Day Ten he is easy prey for Scarlett.
characters.want: To be with Prox and to feel safe. His one real choice is physiologically honest: he can't move himself, so his act is CONSENT ('Pull me, Prox. Gently. I'm scared. Pull me anyway.').
characters.voice: TIP - gentle lyric tenor, warm and boyish, soft floating head voice, playful comic lilt

characters.name: KING PROFUNDUS
characters.who: Prox's father, the great flexor muscle in the forearm castle, with three daughters (middle, ring, little) on one shared muscle belly. He loves by pulling. His recoil dragged Prox into the palm, and his all-out grab on Day Ten nearly tears her. Out of guilt he swears never to pull again, and that frozen vow is Scarlett's best weapon.
characters.want: To keep his daughter safe and close. His arc: pull with everything, then never pull, then 'pull with a whisper'. That phrase is his motif, first prescribed by Thea and finally taught to him by his daughter.
characters.voice: KING PROFUNDUS - booming regal bass-baritone, rich vibrato, commanding but tender underneath

characters.name: SCARLETT ADHESION
characters.who: The villain. She is scar tissue grown where it shouldn't be, the glamorous outlaw queen of No Man's Land, attended by THE FIBROBLASTS, a trio of chorus girls who lay down Type Three collagen 'every which way'. She is half right and knows it: 'every wound sends for me, darling; healing needs me.' She is care that won't let go. She seduces Tip, the guilty King AND Mae Above, whose surgeon's dread of re-rupture she knows. She is nostalgic for three weeks in plaster. She loves the old rubber bands only for the curled-up stiff fingers they left behind. She is the ONLY character who says 'darling'. In the end she is not destroyed but remodelled into aligned Type One: a thin seam 'facing the right way'.
characters.want: To hold Tip, and in the end the whole finger, still forever, glued to the tunnel wall, in the name of safety.
characters.voice: SCARLETT - sultry low contralto, smoky velvet tone, slow purring vibrato, seductive and amused

characters.name: THEA
characters.who: The fairy godmother: Mae's hand therapist and a warm, brisk voice from Above. She turns the theatre plaster into a thermoplastic dorsal blocking splint, teaches place-and-hold, tendon glides and blocking exercises, and reads her goniometer 'wand'. She is the only person Mae can't out-argue ('In here you're not the surgeon, my love. You're the hand.'). Her verbal tics are 'my love', 'lovely' and counting reps, never 'darling'. Gentle rivalry with surgeons: 'The operation took him forty minutes. The next twelve weeks are mine.'
characters.want: For the repair to glide without tearing: little, often and gentle, with a wall at its back.
characters.voice: THEA - warm brassy alto, motherly and witty, brisk swinging phrasing, laughter in the voice

characters.name: LUMBO
characters.who: Comic sidekick. He is the lumbrical, a little worm-shaped muscle growing off Prox's side in the palm, chatty, anxious and sure nobody understands what he does. He is why Prox stopped in the palm and not at the wrist. His big gag in Song 2 is the 'lumbrical plus' finger: whenever the King pulls, the ring finger STRAIGHTENS instead, because the pull now goes through Lumbo.
characters.want: To be appreciated, and to keep Prox from slipping further away. He is finally thanked by name in Song 10.
characters.voice: LUMBO - quick nasal comic tenor, rapid patter, cheeky and fretful

characters.name: DIGBY
characters.who: Comic sidekick. He is the ulnar-side digital nerve of the ring finger ('my side of the family's ulnar'), cut in the same accident and mended last in theatre with thread finer than a hair. His old wires downstream 'packed up and left, but they left me the tunnels'. He regrows about a millimetre a day, and Thea's tap (Tinel's sign) tracks the tingle at his growing front. He is deadpan, laid-back and in no hurry, which is the point.
characters.want: To reach the fingertip by New Year and feel something, even if it's mostly pins and needles.
characters.voice: DIGBY - dry drawling comic baritone, laid-back country twang, deadpan timing

characters.name: THE PULLEYS
characters.who: A comic trio of gatekeepers on the finger tunnel. A2 and A4 are grand Victorian dowagers who know they are the critical ones and treat bowstringing as a public scandal. A1 is deadpan and jaded, cut for trigger finger under local every Tuesday. A3 and A5 share a single sulky line ('Nobody mentions us.').
characters.want: Not to be vented ('a little slit to let her through'), and never to see a bowstring. Their rule: 'A4, or a little of A2, my dear, but NEVER both.'
characters.voice: THE PULLEYS - mock-operetta trio, two grand wobbling dowager sopranos (A2 and A4) and one dry deadpan alto (A1)

characters.name: DR. TEO OKAFOR
characters.who: The surgeon, a calm voice from Above. Mae trained him, and now he repairs her tendon WALANT, wide awake with local anaesthetic and no tourniquet, while she backseat-drives. He hands her own words back to her. In Song 9 he is the voice of the dreaded second operation.
characters.want: Four strands or more, a gap under three millimetres, a glide seen on the table, and for his old teacher to trust him.
characters.voice: DR. TEO - calm warm low baritone, half-spoken, unhurried and kind, gentle humour

characters.name: MAE and WREN
characters.who: MAE owns the hand, and she is a hand surgeon and a terrible patient. She has dry wit, she is controlling and she loves fiercely. She won't let Wren touch the bread knife, says 'hold still' a hundred times a morning, and lies to her therapist. Her list is being covered by colleagues for twelve weeks. WREN is her small daughter, given only two to five words per appearance ('Mum!', 'Bye, Mum!') so the lines survive even if an adult voice sings them.
characters.want: Mae wants her holding hand back for ordinary things: a school lunch, a small hand at the gate, her operating list. Without ever saying it, she must learn to let go of control, of the knife, and of Wren's hand.
characters.voice: MAE - warm adult woman's voice, dry wit, half-spoken, soft untrained alto when singing; WREN - small bright child's voice, very short spoken lines

moral:
THE MORAL, never said aloud: holding on is not the same as keeping. A tendon, a child or a craft stays alive through small, gentle, daily movement inside a protection that still lets it move. You lose it both ways: by gripping too hard, or by holding too still.

HOW IT IS HINTED, NEVER STATED:
(1) Control causes the wound. In Song 1 Mae refuses to let Wren cut her own bagel ('Knives are sharp. Give it here.') and then commits the exact injury she lectures everyone about. No one remarks on the irony.
(2) Two loves that hold too tight, taught only as medical fact. The King's pull tears (Day Ten). His guilty stillness glues (Scarlett). Thea: 'Two ways to lose a tendon: tear it, or glue it.' Biology carries the point: moving tendons mend from the inside, fed by the tunnel's fluid, while still ones get builders from the walls.
(3) Mae's everyday 'hold still' (to a wriggling child in Song 1) is the villain's lullaby (Songs 6 and 7), answered by Thea's 'Place and hold, and then let go' and Tip's 'but nothing ever moves' (Song 9). It returns as a mother tying a shoe at the gate: 'Hold still... done. Go on.' (Song 10). Because it is lyric, Suno carries it.
(4) 'Make a fist for me. / Now open.' moves from Mae's routine catchphrase, to her trainee saying it to her on the table, to a failed command, to the first flicker, and finally to an absent-minded rehab rep Mae does to herself at the school gate as her daughter runs in.
(5) The hero earns it through her father. Prox can't move Tip; only the King can pull. Her victory is teaching him: 'Not like Day Ten. Not like never. Like this.'
(6) Patience comes from the most comic character. Digby's deadpan 'a little further every day, a millimetre, more or less' is about himself only. Prox borrows it.
(7) Wren grows offstage: 'I'll do the bagel, Mum. On the board.' (Song 8), and Mae lets her. This makes the gate earned.
(8) The villain is remodelled, not destroyed ('still here, darling, just facing the right way'). Healing needs scar, pointed the right way.
(9) Guardrails: no one says 'I've learned', no one addresses the audience, and there is no 'believe in yourself'. Every emotional peak sits on a concrete action (a stitch, a tap, a blocking exercise, a shoelace, a fist), and a joke undercuts every swell before it turns sweet. The splint line 'a wall at your back, and an open road ahead' is sung exactly ONCE, literally, by Thea in Song 5, and never explained or reprised.
story:
ACT ONE
(1) THE KINGDOM OF THE HAND. A Tuesday in October, 7:45, in the left hand of Doctor Mae: the holding hand. The kingdom boasts that it has mended a thousand hands and that its owner says 'Make a fist for me. Now open.' to every one of them. She also lectures everyone: never the avocado, never the bagel in your palm. The King pulls from his forearm castle. 'Proxantip', the long-married couple who sing in unison as one, glides 'through the sheath and past the pulleys, one line from the elbow to the fingertip'. Big Sister splits and hugs her from beneath. The pulleys hold her to the bone 'or else she'd bowstring'. Lumbo and Digby get one line each. Above, Mae rushes: 'Wren, hold still!' (sun cream). Wren: 'I can cut it!' Mae: 'Knives are sharp. Give it here.' She holds the bagel in her palm, ring finger curled, and saws. The knife slips. Silence. The unison breaks into 'Tip?' / 'Prox?'. The King roars 'Come home!' and drags Prox into the palm, and as Mae opens her hand Tip slides away down the finger. Digby: 'Half of me's gone quiet.' Mae: 'Look at the cascade. Hold the middle joint. Bend the tip. Nothing. Zone Two. Of course it's Zone Two.'
(2) THE SPACE BETWEEN. That night, in the dark palm. Lumbo held on, which is why Prox stopped here, and every time the King pulls to call her home the finger straightens instead ('Lumbrical plus! Nobody knows what I do, and NOW they do!'). Prox discovers that she and Tip were always two. She refuses her father's 'Come home, stay where it's safe' and vows to go back down through No Man's Land. Lumbo: the surgeon comes on Thursday.
(3) VENT ME NOT. Day one, the finger tunnel. The pulley dowagers panic about being vented tomorrow, treat bowstringing as a Victorian scandal and chaperone the rule (A4 or a little of A2, never both). A1 is bored by Tuesday trigger fingers. Tip shows off his fingertip vanity, then admits he has never moved on his own. Mock-spooky warning from old Doctor Bunnell's map: No Man's Land belongs to SCARLETT ADHESION, who moves into any space that stops moving.
(4) FOUR STRANDS. Day two, theatre, wide awake. Teo, whom Mae trained, draws his lightning-bolt incision, threads Prox back from the palm on a slim children's-ward tube, pins her with a needle like a butterfly, and finds Tip only when he straightens the finger ('There you are. You ran.'). The re-wedding: 'Four strands, Teo.' 'Four's the minimum.' Tip: 'Make it six, if you love me.' The couple are 'never more than three millimetres apart'. 'Make a fist for me': the repair catches on A4, so Teo vents a sliver (Pulleys: 'Only A4! Spare the A2!'). 'Make a fist for me.' Mae: 'I've said that to a thousand patients.' Teo: 'Then you know the next bit. Now open.' It glides. 'Oh. There it is.' A quiet coda: Digby is stitched last with thread finer than a hair, and Mae goes home in plaster, hand held high.
(5) THEA'S RULES. Day three. Thea punctures the glow ('Stitched isn't healed, my love. Stitched is Tuesday.') and redefines the want: the space between that matters now is the tendon and the tunnel wall, a drop of water wide. Plaster becomes a thermoplastic splint, 'a wall at your back, and an open road ahead'. The rules: move early, 'place and hold, and then let go', straight inside the splint and never past it, hand above the heart because swelling is glue, no smoking, no more rubber bands. The weakest days are five to twenty-one. Two ways to lose a tendon: tear it, or glue it. Mae argues: 'In here you're not the surgeon, my love. You're the hand.' To the King: 'Pull with a whisper, Your Majesty.'
(6) DAY TEN (Act One finale). The skin stitches came out today; the tendon ones never will. On the stairs Wren trips ('Mum!'), and Mae grabs her with the splinted hand. The King pulls with everything ('I've got her!'). Prox: 'Not like that, Papa!' The strands creak and hold, just. That night: the King vows never to pull again, Tip begs 'don't move me', Prox pleads 'every hour', Thea's rules echo, and Mae murmurs 'Maybe I'll skip them tonight.' From No Man's Land a velvet voice: 'Hold still, hold still, / nothing tears if nothing moves.' Curtain: tear, or glue?

ACT TWO
(7) HOLD STILL. Weeks three to five. At clinic: 'Doing them every hour?' 'Every hour.' (She isn't.) Scarlett and the Fibroblasts take No Man's Land. She seduces Tip with safety and the guilty King with 'never pull again', and sings up to Mae herself: 'You of all people know what a rupture costs... Hold still, Doctor.' She is nostalgic for three weeks in plaster and for 'those darling rubber bands'. 'There won't be any space between. I'll fill it, darling.' Tip gives in 'just for a while'. Prox begs her father to pull gently; he won't ('I swore'). 'Tip?' No answer.
(8) A MILLIMETRE A DAY. Weeks four to six. Digby's deadpan road trip: old wires gone, tunnels left, the tingle moving each time Thea taps from the tip back towards the repair. Comic postcards: ice lollies, 'ask me next year'. Above, Wren: 'I'll do the bagel, Mum. On the board.' Mae, after a beat: 'Go on, then.' Someone else is doing Mae's Tuesday list. Six weeks: the splint comes off. 'Make a fist for me.' The fingertip won't bend, and the middle and little fingers stop short too. Prox, alone, sings Digby's hook back, sadly.
(9) A LITTLE FURTHER. Week eight, dark. Teo: 'Passive's full, active's nothing. Stuck, not snapped. Three months, then maybe a tenolysis, if she'd do the therapy after.' Mae: 'I am NOT having a tenolysis. Do you know what I tell people about tenolysis?' Beat. 'Right. Every hour.' The King offers to rip Tip loose. Prox: 'That's how a stuck thing snaps. Not like Day Ten. Not like never. Like this.' He learns the whisper. Scarlett: 'Hold still.' Thea: 'Not hold still. Place and hold, and then let go.' Tip: 'Nothing tears if nothing moves, but nothing ever moves. Pull me, Prox. Gently. I'm scared. Pull me anyway.' Thea: 'Hold the middle joint. Bend just the tip.' A flicker. The wand reads five degrees, then ten, twenty, forty: the first bend since the scar set in.
(10) NOW OPEN. Week twelve, a January morning, first day of term. The ring slides back over the knuckle. Walking Wren to school, the finger curls into a full fist round her hand. The King pulls with a whisper and all three daughters close. The pulleys and Lumbo take a joint bow. Digby arrives, more or less ('mostly pins and needles, but it's HER'). Scarlett, remodelled: 'Still here, darling. Just facing the right way.' 'Now we know that we are two, and we glide on the space between.' At the gate: 'Hold still... done. Go on.' Wren: 'Mum, you're doing the weird hand thing again! Bye, Mum!' Hush. Mae, to herself: 'Make a fist for me. Now open.'

motifs.label: THE SPACE BETWEEN (with its ONE LINE verse couplet)
motifs.exact_lyric:
Through the sheath and past the pulleys,
one line from the elbow to the fingertip.
I never knew that we were two
until there was a space between.
motifs.meaning_shift: Two couplets used separately. The first is the ONE LINE couplet (lines 1-2) and the second is the SPACE couplet (lines 3-4). Song 1: Prox and Tip sing the ONE LINE couplet EXACTLY, in unison, as a boast. The third time it breaks off after 'one line from the elbow to the-' at the knife. Song 2: Prox sings the ONE LINE couplet alone with the last word missing ('one line from the elbow to the...'), then introduces the SPACE couplet exactly as the chorus hook. The space is the injury. Song 3: the Pulleys mangle the ONE LINE couplet ('Through the sheath and past the- us, dear. US.'). Song 4: the ONE LINE couplet is sung exactly in HARMONY. The SPACE couplet is sung exactly, then bent to 'Now there's barely a space between, / three millimetres, never more.' Song 5: Thea redefines the space (spoken or sung): 'The space between that matters now / is you and the tunnel wall, a drop of water wide.' Song 7: Scarlett mocks it: 'There won't be any space between. / I'll fill it, darling.' Song 9: Prox bends it to resolve: 'I never knew that we were two / so I'll keep open the space between.' This means keeping the glide space free, never closing a gap. Song 10: the final form is 'Now we know that we are two, / and we glide on the space between.', with the ONE LINE couplet exact in two-part harmony as the finger makes a full fist.

motifs.label: HOLD STILL
motifs.exact_lyric:
Hold still, hold still,
nothing tears if nothing moves.
motifs.meaning_shift: Song 1 (seed, human): Mae, rushing, says to Wren 'Wren, hold still!' (sun cream). It is a parent's everyday phrase, sung and spoken. Song 6: the full couplet, exact and first heard faintly from Scarlett just after the near-tear, when it sounds like comfort and almost like wisdom. Mae can murmur 'hold still' to her own hand just before it. Song 7: the exact couplet as Scarlett's full chorus hook. Variant 'Hold still, Doctor' sung up to Mae. Song 9: Scarlett sings it exactly. Thea answers 'Not hold still. Place and hold, / and then let go.' (planted in Song 5 as 'Place and hold, and then let go.'). Tip turns it: 'Nothing tears if nothing moves, / but nothing ever moves.' Song 10: Mae tying Wren's shoe at the gate: 'Hold still... done. Go on.' The villain's line returns as a mother's ordinary words, followed by release. It is never explained.

motifs.label: MAKE A FIST / NOW OPEN
motifs.exact_lyric:
Make a fist for me.
Now open.
motifs.meaning_shift: Song 1: the chorus boasts that Mae says 'Make a fist for me. Now open.' to a thousand hands. After the cut she self-tests: 'Hold the middle joint. Bend the tip. Nothing.' Song 4: Teo says 'Make a fist for me.' and the repair catches on A4, which is vented. Again: Mae 'I've said that to a thousand patients.' Teo: 'Then you know the next bit. Now open.' It glides. Song 8 (final verse): Thea says 'Make a fist for me.' when the splint comes off, and nothing happens. Song 9: Thea says 'Make a fist for me.' paired with the blocking exercise 'Hold the middle joint. Bend just the tip.' (which echoes Mae's Song 1 self-test), and the first flicker comes. Song 10: the last words of the show, sung softly by Mae to herself as an absent-minded rehab rep after Wren runs in, exactly 'Make a fist for me. / Now open.'

motifs.label: A LITTLE FURTHER
motifs.exact_lyric:
A little further every day,
a millimetre, more or less.
motifs.meaning_shift: Song 8: Digby's deadpan, shrugging road-trip chorus about his own nerve regrowth. At the end of the song Prox sings it alone, slow and sad, after the failed fist. Song 9: Prox takes it as the eleven-o'clock hook, the method for working Tip free, sung first slow and then triumphant after the key change. Song 10: Digby's arrival joke: 'A little further every day... / and here I am. More or less.'

motifs.label: PULL WITH A WHISPER (the King's motif)
motifs.exact_lyric: Pull with a whisper, Your Majesty.
motifs.meaning_shift: Song 5: Thea's comic prescription to the King, who wants to show off his strength. Song 6: forgotten. He pulls with everything ('I've got her!') and Prox cries 'Not like that, Papa!' Song 7: twisted into his frozen vow, 'No pull at all. Not even a whisper.' Scarlett: 'Never pull again, Your Majesty.' Song 9: Prox teaches it back: 'Not like Day Ten. Not like never. Like this.' The King, wondering: 'A whisper. Like this?' Song 10: the King, proud: 'I pull with a whisper now.' All three of his daughters close.

global_sound:
ONE SHARED SOUND WORLD: a lush classic animated-film-musical orchestra with sweeping strings, warm French horns, harp glissandi, celesta and glockenspiel sparkle, clarinet and flute countermelodies, timpani and a rich mixed chorus. It should sound cinematic, warm and polished, with upfront theatrical lead vocals and crisp diction. British English diction throughout.

THREE RECURRING SONIC SIGNATURES (name them in the style prompt of every relevant song):
(1) GLIDE: a rising harp glissando handing off to a smooth legato clarinet line, whenever the tendon moves well.
(2) SCARLETT: low muted trombone, bass clarinet and a slow habanera-tango pulse, whenever she lurks.
(3) TAP: a light woodblock and glockenspiel double tap for Digby, Tinel's taps and Thea's rep counts.

VOICES FROM ABOVE (Mae, Wren, Teo, and Thea when spoken) are closer, drier and half-spoken against the fairytale reverb of the kingdom. Every plot-critical spoken line is ALSO carried in a sung lyric, and every song begins with a sung time stamp ('Day two, the theatre lights...').

Each song keeps the orchestral bed and the same vocal identity descriptions and adds its own genre colour, with the three comic numbers deliberately different from each other. Song 1: pastoral 6/8 into march. Song 2: storybook piano ballad. Song 3: mock-Victorian comic operetta patter. Song 4: romantic waltz. Song 5: big-band swing. Song 6: driving act-finale. Song 7: tango-cabaret. Song 8: bluegrass travel song. Song 9: gospel-tinged power ballad. Song 10: radiant 6/8 reprise anthem. Never name artists, composers, studios, films, songs or shows in style prompts.

songs.title: The Kingdom of the Hand
songs.function: Opening number (ensemble world-builder ending in the inciting incident)
songs.singers: Ensemble chorus; PROX and TIP in unison (as 'Proxantip'); KING PROFUNDUS; THE PULLEYS (one line); LUMBO (one line); DIGBY (one line); MAE (half-sung and spoken from Above); WREN (two short lines)
songs.story_beat: LYRIC BUDGET 3800-4500 characters. Introduce ONLY the King, the couple, the pulleys (one line), Lumbo and Digby (one line each) and Big Sister (one sung half-line). Spend the rest on the bagel set-up and the split. Sung time stamp in the first two lines: 'A Tuesday in October, a quarter to eight, / in the left hand of Doctor Mae.' The chorus calls itself 'the holding hand': it holds the coffee, the phone, the wheel and Wren, and it has mended a thousand hands. The King pulls from his forearm castle (low brass). The couple, introduced as one fused name the kingdom sings, 'Proxantip, so long together they forgot that they were two', sing the ONE LINE couplet in unison. Half-line: 'Big Sister splits and hugs her from beneath.' Pulleys: 'We hold her to the bone, or else she'd bowstring!' Lumbo: 'Nobody knows what I do!' Digby: 'Ulnar side. I feel everything.'
